related_questions.question: How long should you be off work after a positive COVID test?
related_questions.snippet: In accordance with guidance from the CDC, if you test positive for COVID-19 you should: Isolate for 5 days regardless of vaccination status. Only leave isolation after 5 days if you have no symptoms or your symptoms are improving, including at least 24 hours without a fever.

text_blocks.snippet: The latest CDC COVID-19 guidelines emphasize staying up-to-date with vaccinations and taking precautions to protect yourself and others. This includes getting recommended COVID-19 vaccines for the 2024-2025 season, especially for those 6 months and older. The CDC recommends wearing masks and maintaining distance when possible, especially in crowded indoor settings, to reduce transmission. Testing for COVID-19 is also encouraged to help make informed decisions about treatment and further precautions.
